question: A shop offers three successive discounts of 10%, 15% and 20% on a product. Find the single equivalent discount percentage that would result in the same final price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert each discount percentage to its fractional ratio (MP → SP):

10% = 1/10 (10 → 9) | 15% = 3/20 (20 → 17) | 20% = 1/5 (5 → 4)

Net MP = 10 × 20 × 5 = 1000

Net SP = 9 × 17 × 4 = 612

Discount % = (1000 − 612) ÷ 1000 × 100 = 38.8%

**∴ The correct answer is 38.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three successive discounts of 10%, 15%, and 20%.

**Method Used (Base 100):**

Assume the Initial Marked Price (MP) = 100 and apply the discounts sequentially.
